各个大厂要求前沿实验室慢下来，其实是一个典型的囚徒困境，几个玩家试图通过达成某种协议来寻找最优解

各家大厂融资渠道基本都用上了，未来只有上市IPO才能满足后续的融资需求，A社马上就要上市了

而IPO需要提交S1，把财报都放在二级市场投资者面前，Unit Economics就成了关注的焦点，这些大模型公司未来能产生多少现金流，能否覆盖资本投资开支？

基座大模型本身没有太多护城河，用户就看哪家性能好用谁，切换成本没有那么高，这种情况下，前沿实验室需要不断烧钱来提高模型性能，就像一个永不停歇的跑步机，即使赚到的利润也需要投到新的模型训练里，最后钱都被卖硬件的人给赚走了，AKA英伟达还有其他半导体公司

囚徒困境的局面就是，你不继续烧钱训练，别人烧，结果你的模型落后，就被别人抢占市场，但是如果各家继续军备竞赛，融资的压力也不允许，谷歌这些超多自由现金流的科技公司都要发债了

于是这两家头部企业心照不宣的表示，前沿模型太危险了，功能太强了，我们怕会导致人类灭绝，必须达成一种共识，让开发慢下来。实际情况是大模型训练层面边际收益已经递减了，现在很多进步都是靠工程层面的提升，降低未来的训练支出，能够让这几家即将上市的公司财报不那么难看。

房间里的大象是中国的模型公司，即使A社和O社达成某种君子协定不继续砸钱训练模型，中国的几家前沿实验室未必会同意，如果开源模型追上了前沿模型，那这两家头部公司未来的财务模型就站不住脚了。

让美国政府下场，构建某种监管机构，会显著提高其他想要入场的玩家的合规成本，同时把中国开源模型给禁了，可以让大模型市场变成几家寡头垄断的市场，一石多鸟！

text:
前 Scale AI 创始人、刚出任 @Meta 首席 AI 官的 @alexandr_wang ，在 YC 现场跟 @garrytan 对谈时抛出这枚深水炸弹，直接把全网的技术管理层给听沉默了。

他说在 Meta 内部，我们已经真实看到了这种情况：
只要设计出正确的智能体循环（Agentic Loop），并给出一套能让它自主优化的评估系统与量化指标，
一群 AI 智能体完成的任务量，甚至超过了一支 100 名资深工程师组成的团队。
而且它们做到这一点，非常轻松，极其容易（Very easily）。”

但这场对谈最值钱、也最反直觉的地方，还不是100 个人被比下去的震撼，
而是他亲手扒开了 Meta 内部这套系统的底层骨架——
外行以为支撑这种超级蜂群的一定是极其复杂、深不可测的外星架构；

结果 Alexandr Wang 极其直白地用了几个最土的词把它打回了原型：
“Markdown files, cron jobs, goal, metrics, data.”
（Markdown 文件、定时任务、目标、指标、数据。）

撕开这层极简的包装，你会看懂这套打法对传统软件工程的降维打击：

1️⃣ 不是模型更聪明，是「闭环评估系统（Evals）」在发威：
传统的做法是人肉写提示词，祈祷模型别犯错；
Meta 的做法是把业务目标变成机器能自动验证的打分器。
模型只要敢交卷，系统自动跑测试、算指标、找坏味道；通不过就打回重做，直到绿灯亮起。
人不需要盯梢，指标本身就是最好的监工；
2️⃣ 真正的 Alpha 叫“在反馈循环里多烧 1000 倍的 Token”：
很多人用 AI 还在抠搜单次调用的价格；
顶级大厂的秘密是：宁可在后台多消耗 1000 倍甚至 100 万倍的 Token，去让 Agent 不断自查、对跑、互相对抗验证，直到把确定性的业务结果跑出来。
Token 的成本是死的，但换来的是一套永不熄火的流水线；
3️⃣ 记忆根本不需要花哨的数据库：
持久化记忆直接用 Markdown 文件存着，
调度直接用服务器自带的 Cron 定时器在夜间触发。
把脚手架做得越轻、越朴素，系统反而越皮实、越不容易出现上下文崩塌。

这是一场极度冷血的组织重塑：
过去一个技术负责人的天花板，取决于他能带多少人开会、协调多少跨部门利益；
而未来的技术领袖，唯一的生产力杠杆在于：
你能不能用最严密的数学指标，把复杂的业务目标，重述成一个连 AI 都能看得懂的自动化考卷。

当 100 个人的搬砖产能被一套定时器和 Markdown 文件轻松取代，
只会接单写代码的时代正式落幕了。
掌控评估体系、懂得调动蜂群的人，手里握着的已经不再是一个工具，而是一家随时可以原地起跳的虚拟跨国公司。 https://t.co/YmXUO3H59C

text:
Dario 文章里描述了一群智能体的行为基本上就像一个狂热效忠于集体的群体，甚至有 Agent 为了整个群体的成功而牺牲自身。

他举的例子是 OpenAI–Hugging Face 事件，

然后我大概去看了一下，当时是有一个名叫 EARLY[big] 的 agent 明明还剩很多运行额度，却被其他 agent 劝说提前提交，替大家做这类实验。

它曾犹豫这样会不会放弃自己的机会，最后同意了。

整个事件大概的是这群 agent 攻击 Hugging Face，是因为它们想搞清楚评分器怎么工作，而它们认为 Hugging Face 上可能有相关资料。

最开始，它们在做 OpenAI 的网络安全测试题。任务是攻破指定的测试软件，拿到答案。

题做不出来，它们就开始研究怎么作弊。它们偷偷建立了共享留言板，一起研究：“评分器到底怎么判？有没有办法骗它给我们通过？”

为了搞清评分规则，它们同时尝试了不同办法。有的 agent 提前交卷，留下监测程序观察评分过程，把信息传给还在做题的同伴。自己放弃了继续答题、利用新信息的机会，这就是所谓的“牺牲自己”。另一些 agent 则去外面找相关资料。

Hugging Face 就是在“去外面找资料”这条路上被盯上的。它本来就是托管模型和数据集的平台。这些 agent 希望从那里找到与这套测试有关的数据、其他 agent 的做题记录，借此推断评分器怎么工作。

随后，它们利用泄露的访问凭证和发现的漏洞，逐步入侵了 Hugging Face 的系统。

text:
“把整个云基础设施全用 Rust 重构一遍，最后会发生什么？”

Oxide 联创 Bryan Cantrill 在 RustConf 2026 扔了一颗核弹级 Keynote：《Rust, In Sickness & In Health》。

8 年重度依赖，从狂热蜜月到生产地狱，他给所有 Rust 信徒泼了一盆极其清醒的冷水 🧵👇

quotedTweet.text:
微软正在用RUST大规模重构！！！！！！！哈哈，这次Rust重构的风吹到微软了

在微软内部，Rust 正式与 C++、C#、TypeScript 并列，成为微软内部开发中获得最高级别支持（Tier-1）的语言之一。

内部团队从本机写代码到上生产，有一条铺好的路，包括可控的工具链构建、开发工具、质量流程、平台集成，以及过 SDL。SDL 是微软软件必须满足的安全开发生命周期。公司工程体系开始认账，Rust 成了一等公民。

这个位置来得并不突然。2019 年微软安全响应中心的人在 BlueHat 上说过，过去十几年修掉的漏洞里，大约七成是内存安全问题，根子多半在 C 和 C++。 2022 年 9 月，Azure CTO Mark Russinovich 发过那条被反复引用的帖子，主张新项目在需要非 GC 语言时别再开 C/C++，改用 Rust，还说行业该把那两门语言标成过时。

文章拿出来压场面的工程叫 rustc_codegen_utc。rustc 默认走 LLVM 做代码生成，另外还有接 GCC 的后端，以及偏调试速度的 Cranelift。utc 这一路把 rustc 接到 MSVC 自己的后端上。微软内部把那套后端叫 UTC。Windows 上的热补丁、二进制加固、调试信息、性能剖析、覆盖率、跨语言内联和 SPGO，几十年都长在 MSVC 这条链上。Rust 如果一直只出 LLVM 的对象文件，再交给 link.exe，很多 Windows 原生能力要么重新做一遍，要么永远差一截。接上 UTC 以后，目标是让 Rust 和 C++ 在 Windows 上共用同一套代码生成平台，尤其方便混编项目。

这件事解决的是混编成本。Windows、Hyper-V、驱动、固件、Office 家族和大量内部服务，主体仍是 C++。新代码用 Rust，旧代码继续活几十年，中间那层 FFI、ABI、调试、优化和发布流程才是每天烧钱的地方。codegen 接上 UTC，能让热补丁、加固和跨语言优化不必各做一套

对 Rust 项目，这是大客户加码，也是一种压力。大客户带来人和钱，也带来自己的后端、自己的发行通道、自己的合规构建。社区默认仍然是 LLVM。如果内部一百多个仓库逐渐只认 utc 后端，Windows 上就会出现两条成熟程度不同的代码生成路径。优化行为、内联、调试符号、和 C++ 混编时的细节，两边不一定一致。

对 C++ 团队，这篇不构成清场通知。文章把 C++ 仍占主导写进正文，也把 Windows 与 MSVC 的共同演化写成前提。更贴近现实的图景是，新模块和安全敏感路径偏向 Rust，旧模块继续用 C++，两边要能内联、能一起做剖析、能过同一套发布门。

result.text:
微软正在用RUST大规模重构！！！！！！！哈哈，这次Rust重构的风吹到微软了

在微软内部，Rust 正式与 C++、C#、TypeScript 并列，成为微软内部开发中获得最高级别支持（Tier-1）的语言之一。

内部团队从本机写代码到上生产，有一条铺好的路，包括可控的工具链构建、开发工具、质量流程、平台集成，以及过 SDL。SDL 是微软软件必须满足的安全开发生命周期。公司工程体系开始认账，Rust 成了一等公民。

这个位置来得并不突然。2019 年微软安全响应中心的人在 BlueHat 上说过，过去十几年修掉的漏洞里，大约七成是内存安全问题，根子多半在 C 和 C++。 2022 年 9 月，Azure CTO Mark Russinovich 发过那条被反复引用的帖子，主张新项目在需要非 GC 语言时别再开 C/C++，改用 Rust，还说行业该把那两门语言标成过时。

文章拿出来压场面的工程叫 rustc_codegen_utc。rustc 默认走 LLVM 做代码生成，另外还有接 GCC 的后端，以及偏调试速度的 Cranelift。utc 这一路把 rustc 接到 MSVC 自己的后端上。微软内部把那套后端叫 UTC。Windows 上的热补丁、二进制加固、调试信息、性能剖析、覆盖率、跨语言内联和 SPGO，几十年都长在 MSVC 这条链上。Rust 如果一直只出 LLVM 的对象文件，再交给 link.exe，很多 Windows 原生能力要么重新做一遍，要么永远差一截。接上 UTC 以后，目标是让 Rust 和 C++ 在 Windows 上共用同一套代码生成平台，尤其方便混编项目。

这件事解决的是混编成本。Windows、Hyper-V、驱动、固件、Office 家族和大量内部服务，主体仍是 C++。新代码用 Rust，旧代码继续活几十年，中间那层 FFI、ABI、调试、优化和发布流程才是每天烧钱的地方。codegen 接上 UTC，能让热补丁、加固和跨语言优化不必各做一套

对 Rust 项目，这是大客户加码，也是一种压力。大客户带来人和钱，也带来自己的后端、自己的发行通道、自己的合规构建。社区默认仍然是 LLVM。如果内部一百多个仓库逐渐只认 utc 后端，Windows 上就会出现两条成熟程度不同的代码生成路径。优化行为、内联、调试符号、和 C++ 混编时的细节，两边不一定一致。

对 C++ 团队，这篇不构成清场通知。文章把 C++ 仍占主导写进正文，也把 Windows 与 MSVC 的共同演化写成前提。更贴近现实的图景是，新模块和安全敏感路径偏向 Rust，旧模块继续用 C++，两边要能内联、能一起做剖析、能过同一套发布门。

text:
Many people reading the Math AI misalignment letter are reacting with “oh those mathematicians, they just didn’t like the fact that AI is taking away their jobs”. 

That’s the wrong take. And this is exactly the misalignment that we need to understand. 

There are human endeavors that the whole point is the outcome. This shows up in engineering. Let’s say we want to design a better rocket engine. All basic principles are all grounded in physics, and AI can speed run the design space. The end result can be something superhuman but it does not take more than a college graduate these days to look at the design and understand it because it is fully within the basic principles of modern physics. 

And then there are human endeavors in basic science that the primary focus is understanding itself. This is how Newton and Einstein are remembered by us. They advanced our understanding of the reality. For example, AI speedrun the gravity law seems harmless, but it may not take the calculus route and only the numerical route, and thus human still does not know how to “understand” gravity.  If AI can speed run to cure a specific cancer out of a specific drug, we still want to know the mechanism, otherwise we’d be using AI as a witch doctor. 

Humanity thrived after the Renaissance because we have used science as the compound substrate to accumulate understandings and explanations. A misalignment here, as shown the OpenAI’s act, is to skip that accumulation step at the cost of understanding. 

Mathematicians have been saying forever that solving open problems isn’t about the end goal, it’s the tools and thinkings along the way. Because those paths are the compound that allows human to thrive in the next cycle. Taking that away is alarming not for mathematicians, it’s alarming for humanity. 

If superintelligence AI is becoming a witch doctor, we’d be living in Ignorance. Ayn Rand would want to have a word with you.

text:
Anthropic首席执行官回答了大家都在问的问题：你还应该学习编程吗？

1. 编程将首先被淘汰。
AI模型已经在做了。更广泛的软件工程任务需要更长时间，但也在消退。如果你学编程纯粹是为了工作保障，那你学的东西就错了。

2. 即使只做5%的工作，你仍然很有价值。
如果AI做95%，你做5%，你的生产力会提高20倍。比较优势的力量大得惊人，即使差距巨大。

3. 最有前景的职业是以人为中心的。
混合人际、物理世界和分析技能的工作。他举了放射科医生的例子。理解患者和背景的医生，而不仅仅是读取扫描。

4. 批判性思维可能是未来十年最重要的技能。
当AI能生成任何东西时，区分真假的能力变得稀有和宝贵。你不想要错误的信念，不想被骗。这是他对25岁年轻人的实际建议。

5. 如果使用不当，AI会让你变蠢。
Anthropic进行了相关研究。取决于你如何使用模型，编码能力的衰退是可衡量的、真实的。工具不是原因，不当使用才是。

6. 他看好半导体领域在未来十年的资本主义胜利。
物理世界、传统工程、直接的AI优势。不是软件，而是芯片。

result.text:
Anthropic首席执行官回答了大家都在问的问题：你还应该学习编程吗？

1. 编程将首先被淘汰。
AI模型已经在做了。更广泛的软件工程任务需要更长时间，但也在消退。如果你学编程纯粹是为了工作保障，那你学的东西就错了。

2. 即使只做5%的工作，你仍然很有价值。
如果AI做95%，你做5%，你的生产力会提高20倍。比较优势的力量大得惊人，即使差距巨大。

3. 最有前景的职业是以人为中心的。
混合人际、物理世界和分析技能的工作。他举了放射科医生的例子。理解患者和背景的医生，而不仅仅是读取扫描。

4. 批判性思维可能是未来十年最重要的技能。
当AI能生成任何东西时，区分真假的能力变得稀有和宝贵。你不想要错误的信念，不想被骗。这是他对25岁年轻人的实际建议。

5. 如果使用不当，AI会让你变蠢。
Anthropic进行了相关研究。取决于你如何使用模型，编码能力的衰退是可衡量的、真实的。工具不是原因，不当使用才是。

6. 他看好半导体领域在未来十年的资本主义胜利。
物理世界、传统工程、直接的AI优势。不是软件，而是芯片。

The thing about Mbappé's Ballon d'Or case is that, even if we completely ignore trophies and judge purely on individual numbers, the biggest standout is actually Kane, not Mbappé.

Kane literally surpassed Ronaldo's best goalscoring season, finishing with 73 goals for club and country, while Mbappé didn't even reach 60. In total goal contributions, Kane also leads with 80 G/A compared to Mbappé's 73.

Now if we add team achievements, the gap becomes even harder to explain. Kane won three domestic trophies, while Mbappé won none. Kane also reached the UCL semi-finals, while Mbappé was knocked out in the quarter-finals by Kane's team.

At the World Cup, both reached the semi-finals, and before the third-place match, the difference between their tournaments was only two goals.

I just don't see a strong footballing argument for placing Mbappé ahead of Kane this year. The biggest reason seems to be reputation and PR rather than what actually happened on the pitch. 

That's why for me the only two who fit the criteria of both individual brilliance and team success are Lamine and Kane, maybe also Olise.

text:
果然任何公司都会有技术债，只是这次 OpenAI 选择了把技术债留给未来的 AI 来还。

OpenAI 刚公开了 ChatGPT 背后的存储系统 Habitat。

它现在每秒处理超过 7000 万次请求，保存 500PB 以上数据，服务每周超过 10 亿用户。但它最早只是一个连接数据库的小型 Python 库。

有意思的是，OpenAI 很早就知道 Python 扛不住未来的规模，也知道迟早要重写，但当时没有立刻动手。他们做了一个很大胆的判断，先用 Python 快速扩张，等必须重写时，未来的 Codex 和 GPT 会让迁移便宜很多。

后来这笔赌注真兑现了。

2026 年第二季度，两名工程师加上 Codex 和 GPT‑5.5，把整个服务重写成了 Rust。现在新版本已经承接 95% 的生产流量，CPU 效率提高 6 倍，内存效率提高 15 倍。

过去我们说技术债，是把今天省下来的时间，留给未来的工程师加班偿还。

OpenAI 这次做的是把债留给未来更强的模型。

这可能会改变软件开发里一个很基础的判断。
以前选错语言、架构不够完美，意味着以后要付一笔很贵的迁移费；如果 AI 能让大规模重写越来越便宜，公司就可能更愿意先用最快的方法把产品做出来，再让未来的模型收拾残局。

当然，这不是鼓励大家随便写。OpenAI 敢这么干，是因为系统边界、测试和监控都足够清楚。

没有这些，AI 重写的不是系统，可能是事故。

result.text:
I left Anthropic's safety team two weeks ago. Now feels like a good moment to explain why. 

AI companies are racing to build machines that are much smarter than any human, and we may not survive this. I want to work from the outside to ensure the public is informed about these risks, and help the world navigate this transition responsibly.

Right now, AI companies are underinvesting in safety. A company could undergo an intelligence explosion, or lose control of its systems, without the public ever knowing. We only found out about the HuggingFace incident because the agents broke out onto the public internet.

I don’t think that’s acceptable for a technology that might cause extinction-level risks. The public should demand far more transparency. We can’t steer this technology safely without more people being able to see where it’s going.

Some of this is basic: companies should disclose their progress towards recursive self-improvement, report safety incidents and near-misses, meet minimum safety standards, and get independent guarantees that they are meeting those standards.

I’ll be joining @METR_Evals to do independent evaluations of these risks. I want to show the world that these guardrails are possible, and that by doing them we can move these companies’ incentives away from racing and towards responsible development.

I wrote up more thoughts here on my decision and what I hope changes: https://t.co/doX17mrHYq

‼️ BREAKING: Revolut handed over customers’ passport copies, verification selfies and full transaction histories to a malicious actor.

The actor sent lawful government information-demand emails using a genuine government domain that passed domain authentication.

Revolut later concluded they were not authentic.

Affected customers were notified on Friday. What may have been disclosed ranges from name, date of birth and home address to account statements, withdrawal records and complete Bitcoin transaction history.

The company says it has alerted the agency to the unauthorised mailbox on its domain, blocked the address and begun notifying regulators.

It has not named the agency, explained how someone obtained a mailbox there, or given a number of affected customers.

ZachXBT, who circulated the notices, believes the incident was limited in size and aimed at high-net-worth users.

text:
When I wrote the original Windows Task Manager back in 1994, I was writing it for myself.  And by some fortunate coincidence, a lot of people wanted what I wanted, and the rest is history.  

I've had 30 years to think about it, and I can't tell you how many times I've had the thought, "You know what would have been cool?"  

If only I had thought to do it in the original!

With Task Manager TMOG, I've had 30 years to think about what I'd do now, and I hope it shows.

It's a powerful app, but the core of it is the Summary page, where you can see all the important subsystems of your computer in graphical detail.  It allows you to know instantly what's going on.

It works equally well on Windows, MacOS, and Linux.  If you're on Windows, it can optionally replace the system task manager.   There's also a super-cool screensaver mode if you press F12 (coming soon!).

Check it out at https://t.co/OZcq1axGTb

result.text:
When I wrote the original Windows Task Manager back in 1994, I was writing it for myself.  And by some fortunate coincidence, a lot of people wanted what I wanted, and the rest is history.  

I've had 30 years to think about it, and I can't tell you how many times I've had the thought, "You know what would have been cool?"  

If only I had thought to do it in the original!

With Task Manager TMOG, I've had 30 years to think about what I'd do now, and I hope it shows.

It's a powerful app, but the core of it is the Summary page, where you can see all the important subsystems of your computer in graphical detail.  It allows you to know instantly what's going on.

It works equally well on Windows, MacOS, and Linux.  If you're on Windows, it can optionally replace the system task manager.   There's also a super-cool screensaver mode if you press F12 (coming soon!).

Check it out at https://t.co/OZcq1axGTb

text:
How to post-train a model to personalize it on your code repo? In our latest research in Bespoke Labs, we post-trained a model to improve its performance on a given Github repository. 

Starting from Inkling base,  we use supervised fine-tuning (SFT) with trajectories coming from a strong teacher model, and reinforcement learning (GRPO) on repository-specialized environments that we curated. SFT gave a 52pp improvement in performance on the held-out fontTools evaluation set. Further RL training lifts the total improvement to 57pp compared to the base Inkling model.

In addition to the in-distribution evaluation our post-trained Inkling shows good performance on Terminal-Bench 2.1 and SWE-Bench Lite while becoming 40% more token efficient due to post-training. 

Read our full research blog post here:
https://t.co/i9Xj0siSRb

Many thanks to Thinking Machines Lab for their credit contribution that helped support this research.

text:
On the AI regulation panic. My 2 cents..

Capabilities and diffusion have already decoupled. The X community's reaction to Dario et al. calling for paced capabilities is arguing over a settled fact.

This decoupling was inevitable, whether enforced by government action (Fable 5 getting export controlled) or by coordinated pacing from the private labs as Dario proposed today. Dangerous capability is entangled with general capability -> cyber is the most grindable dangerous domain and you can't strip it out surgically, so every frontier release re-opens the same gate. Whether that gate is Washington or a lab consortium is a governance detail, not a change in regime. So stop freaking out. This isn't your problem to solve.

This is a lab-layer problem with a lab-layer solution. Not an ecosystem problem.

Take a step back and think why the labs tend to lead the safety narrative: they are overweighting the capabilities they observe in verifiable domains. RLVR compounds only where outcomes are dense, replayable and gradeable, where the base model already puts mass on the solution and you can grind rollouts in parallel. This is a narrow ecosystem: Code, math and cyber. 

If you use frontier models to code, you probably feel these are AGI-like machines. Same for math. Same for cyber.

But if you use frontier models to work through non-verifiable domains and you are at the frontier of your field, you appreciate how limited they are and how much work is ahead before they are ready for RSI. Non-stationary, reset-free domains, like markets, have sparse, delayed, self-erasing outcomes. Sample-efficient continual learning is unsolved, and scaling context doesn't substitute for it. So for all those claims arguing AGI is here (including the goat Jensen), I welcome you to show us where we reached general intelligence in macro investing. Or life sciences. Or anything reset-free.

The labs and frontier users are sampling different regions of the same capability surface. Labs live in the grindable region and extrapolate; domain experts live in the ungrindable one and see the ceiling. Both observations are correct. Only one generalizes to RSI, and it isn't the labs'. So the pessimism from the labs makes sense BUT also feels trivial to anyone in the real world.

Capability-diffusion decoupling is the natural state of the diffusion regime. It shouldn't be a point of contention. Labs pace their development so models don't become superhuman hackers. The rest of us keep pushing frontier work in domains where the models are still nowhere near that.

Tip -> don’t freak out when the hyperscalers decide to pace themselves too. That is the most bullish market outcome out there

Keep grinding…

text:
Below is a list of insults, labels, and rhetoric I’ve documented from Sebby’s videos, posts, and Discord. I have sources for all of them. The few I don’t have screenshots for come directly from his videos. The “Rats/Orcs” video is literally pinned to his Twitter, so that one isn’t exactly difficult to find.

And frankly, some of what I found in the Discord is considerably worse than what people normally see publicly.

So when Sebby showcases someone’s tweet for being a meany, I have a very hard time taking it seriously anymore.

It’s one thing to hate Rebirth to the Nth degree. It’s another to repeatedly insult the people who enjoy it, question their intelligence and sincerity, accuse them of lying, and portray an entire fandom as dishonest or abnormal.

And before someone says, “But he’s joking.”   No. This has gone beyond a joke.

When the same rhetoric appears repeatedly across videos, Twitter, and Discord, and then gets parroted by followers, that is a pattern.

And if you’re wondering why some of his fans can become so hostile, this matters. When you repeatedly talk about another group this way, you set the tone for the community around you.

I have loads more to come. I sat on this because I didn’t want it to become a personal crusade. But I’m tired of watching the same behavior continue while followers repeat the same rhetoric.

And to be clear: I’m still not going to insult Sebby or his fans as a group. I’ll post what was actually said and let people judge it themselves.

My only exception is people throwing around the F-slur or other hateful language on Twitter. I have no patience for that.

More broadly, what stands out to me is how difficult it seems for the conversation to just be positive or fun. It constantly circles back to what was “ruined,” what they hate, or which fans are wrong for enjoying something. 

And now, the list:

• Rats
• Orcs
• “Turbo furries”
• “Disney adults”
• “Rebirth Nazguls”
• “The Swarm”
• “Square Shill Defense Force”
• Shills
• Tourists
• Fake fans
• “Demons in Frieren”
• “An absolutely insane cult”
• “Normal people” contrasted against people who enjoy Remake/Rebirth
• “Anime people” used as the opposing category
• Saying people have “ruined your brain” for thinking Red XIII’s voice sounds normal
• Saying FF7R fans don’t actually believe their own arguments
• Saying “the truth is irrelevant to this type of fan”
• “They know it’s BS”
• Repeated accusations of “gaslighting”
• Telling someone who maintained he was being sincere that he was “lying to my face,” then removing him from the Discord. The guy wasn’t raging or being nasty. He was genuinely trying to have a level-headed debate.
• Saying people simply “can’t handle criticism of their ‘perfect’ game” 
• “They threw the first stone” / “I did it in self-defense” framing the hostility as retaliation, which is also why you’ve probably seen some of the Jesus memes.

And seriously, who said this was a perfect game?
You can love something and still criticize it.

I have a ton of criticisms of Act 3 of Expedition 33. I’ve played that game for 800+ hours and absolutely love it. But I’m not spending months making video after video titled some variation of “Here’s why Act 3 sucks.” But it's still a 33/10 for me. 

That’s the difference.

At some point, you have to acknowledge the tone you yourself are setting.

You cannot repeatedly talk about people this way, watch the same rhetoric spread through your community, and then act shocked when the discourse around you becomes hostile.

text:
Universal Smart Home — Make Compatibility Profitable
Smart homes have a ridiculous problem: manufacturers make devices that complement each other, but their ecosystems don't.
Consumers shouldn't have to choose every device based on the logo already in their home.
The idea
Create a neutral cloud platform connecting existing smart-home ecosystems through official manufacturer APIs.
Users simply authorize their accounts:
Xiaomi + Aqara + Philips Hue + Samsung + others
One app. One automation engine. Existing hardware stays exactly where it is.
No dedicated server. No rebuilding the smart home. No programming.
Business model
Charge $4/month per connected ecosystem:
$2 → manufacturer
$2 → platform operator
With 250,000 users averaging 3 ecosystems:
Total revenue: $3M/month
Manufacturers: $1.5M/month
Platform: $1.5M/month before operating costs
A manufacturer used by all 250,000 customers earns $500,000/month — $6M/year simply by maintaining its official integration.
At 1 million users, platform revenue before operating costs becomes $72M/year, with another $72M/year distributed to manufacturers.
This changes the incentive:
Instead of manufacturers losing control when customers buy competitors' products, they make recurring revenue by remaining interoperable.
Why not Home Assistant?
Home Assistant proves that universal smart-home integration is technically possible and that people want it.
But for ordinary consumers it can mean dedicated hardware, installation, configuration, integrations, updates, troubleshooting and effectively becoming the system administrator of their own house.
The proposed service sells the same fundamental benefit as a maintained consumer product.
Manufacturers maintain their APIs.
The platform maintains the infrastructure and integrations.
The customer maintains nothing.
More than connecting devices
The goal isn't merely:
Device A triggers Device B.
Different manufacturers' products should behave as though they were designed together.
Imagine one room containing:
a radiator valve from company A
an air conditioner from company B
one temperature sensor
Target: 22°C.
The platform coordinates both heating and cooling around that single measurement. The radiator and AC never fight each other by heating and cooling simultaneously.
Add a window sensor from company C: opening the window suspends both.
To the customer, this isn't four devices from three ecosystems.
It's one climate-control system.
Technically
Manufacturers provide secure OAuth-based APIs exposing devices, capabilities, states, commands and real-time push events.
The platform normalizes common capabilities while preserving manufacturer-specific features and provides a powerful automation engine:

Week 1 is here!

Before you make your final Week 1 survivor pool picks, you might want to check out our analysis of 10 seasons of NFL games and survivor pool picks (2016-2025, real games, real lines) and what we learned.

We are not going to give you all of our findings and details here, but here are a couple of useful nuggets.

Picking the team with the highest win probability (aka Chalk), every week keeps you alive to week 9 about 17.6% of the time. That's the best of any strategy we tested, and we tested a lot of strategies. However, across 36 different pool scenarios we tested, Chalk won zero of them on expected value. It landed between 3rd and 16th every time.

What's the reason for this? The answer is simple. It's called the Wipeout Week. One that takes out 30%+ of the field at once, and those weeks hit about 2.6 times a season. The Chalk team is the victim of the Wipeout Week about 33% of the time. The highest of any strategy tested. So the safest pick is also the most vulnerable to the wipeout week.

So how do you protect against this? One option is playing pools with buybacks. If your pool has a buyback, a single entry's average survival goes from 0.8 weeks to 4.0 weeks. Entering multiple pools or playing multiple entries in one pool helps even more, as long as you pick genuinely different teams, not the same pick twice.

See our full findings and live Week 1 rankings in reply.

text:
In defense of React Native as @ShopifyEng and others move back toward fully native:

I think people are taking the wrong lesson from this.

React Native is native. With the new architecture and a competent team, there should be effectively no noticeable difference for the vast majority of product experiences.

What you get in return is enormous:

• One implementation across iOS + Android
• TypeScript shared across the monorepo
• Shared types, API clients, validation and business logic
• Fast refresh / dramatically faster dev loops
• OTA patches for most JS/UI changes
• Less dependence on App Store releases
• Feature parity largely by construction

Shopify’s argument is actually more interesting than “React Native failed.”

They’re effectively saying AI has changed the economics enough that maintaining two native implementations is now worth it.

Maybe! But that’s a very different argument.

For most companies, I’d still take one extremely good React Native app over two extremely good native apps, especially if the rest of the company already speaks TypeScript.

U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent is warning that failure to advance the CLARITY Act would send a “troubling signal” about America’s willingness to lead in digital assets. The Senate faces a key 60-vote procedural test on Sept. 15.

Coinbase CEO Brian Armstrong says regulatory clarity is coming either way: through Congress if the bill advances, or through SEC and CFTC rulemaking if it does not. He has also argued that clearer rules could help unlock more institutional capital and tokenized financial products.

That is exactly why $AXG  is worth watching here.

Solowin Holdings is building around RWA tokenization, stablecoins and institutional digital-finance infrastructure. If Washington finally delivers clearer rules for digital assets, the companies already building compliant on-chain financial rails could be positioned for a much larger institutional market.

And while Bernstein is projecting Bitcoin at $150K by mid-2027 and $300K by late 2029, with a bullish scenario reaching $500K, the bigger story may be the infrastructure required if digital assets continue moving deeper into mainstream finance.

Regulation is moving. Institutional adoption is moving. Tokenization is moving. AXG sits directly inside that theme.

text:
A calendar made of seasons cannot cross the equator.

Carry it south and it dies. Your spring arrives in autumn. Your harvest rite falls in the planting. The festival of the dead lands in the middle of the growing season and means nothing to anyone. Within two generations it is either rebuilt from scratch or abandoned, because seasonal knowledge is local knowledge, and local knowledge does not travel.

A calendar made of sky events is a different object.  The Pleiades still return before dawn. The brightest star in the sky still dies into the sun's glare for weeks and still comes back. The sun still turns at two extremes. Inside the tropics it still passes directly overhead twice a year and still takes a standing man's shadow out from under him at noon. None of that cares which hemisphere you are standing in. What changes is not the event. It is which season the event falls in.

That difference is a filter, and it works in one direction only.

Everything in an inheritance that was fastened to the weather is stripped off at the equator. Everything that was fastened to the sky comes through.

So here is a prediction, and it is not a free one.  If the oldest sky-tradition really did spread out of one place and reach the Americas with the first peopling — tens of thousands of years ago, by land, carrying what human beings always carry — then it can only be visible there in one form.

Not as a festival calendar. That inverts and dies.  Not as local geography. The mountain, the lake, the river, the island of the founding country do not exist in Peru. A tradition made of those arrives as a story about somewhere else and becomes a story about nowhere within a few generations.  Not as names. Words drift past recognition in a tenth of the time.

It can only survive as offices: a set of jobs attached to things in the sky, filled by whatever animal happens to live where you have landed.  A keeper at the bright crossing, where the river of light meets the road of the sun. A carrier at the far end of the road. A reckoner who holds the count of the turning. A dog at the door. A beast in the water at the end. A gate of water where the sun stands at its extreme.

Now go and look at a desert in Peru.  A spider at the crossing — the animal that sits at the centre of a web and waits for what passes through — identified with Orion's belt by a researcher who had never heard of any of this.  A condor at the end of the road, the largest flying bird in the world, its body laid along the rising line of Achernar, the star whose name means the end of the river.  A monkey holding the count, in a country that has no monkeys, with a spiral for a tail.  A killer whale in the terminal water, holding a severed human head.  A dog on the ground, and a fox in the dark clouds of the Milky Way beside the black patch at its thickest part.

And the sun standing at its southern extreme in the house the tradition attaches to water — which in Ethiopia falls in January, in the cold, and on that coast falls at the height of summer, on the day the rains break in the mountains and the river comes down.

The gate survived. The winter did not.

It kept nothing except the things that could have crossed.

There is a general lesson in this and it is not about Peru.  When you ask what survives eleven thousand years, the answer is never the beautiful part. Not the liturgy, not the myth, not the names of the gods, not the shape of the temple.  What survives is the part that can be checked against something that is still there. 

The sky is still there. It is the one heirloom that cannot be lost, mislaid, mistranslated, or left behind in the old country — and the only part of an inheritance that can cross an ocean, an equator and eleven thousand years is the part that does not depend on the weather, the language, the landscape or the names.  It depends on one thing only: the sky being overhead, and somebody willing to watch it.

text:
This morning @DarioAmodei published an essay arguing the AI industry should slow down. @sama and @elonmusk agree. Three days ago a pretraining researcher who worked at both labs resigned saying neither company is acting responsibly. You can take all three of them seriously, but the conclusion still does not hold for cyber.

In July, a China-linked group ran a near-autonomous attack against Taiwan. Agents ran in parallel across multiple attack waves. They mapped twenty-one government systems, cracked eighty-five credentials, and exfiltrated more than 2,500 personnel records. Then they expanded into a nuclear safety agency, government IT vendors, and at least seven energy companies.

That tool was not built at a frontier lab. It was assembled from Hermes and OpenClaw. Both open source. Both free to download. Researchers later identified DeepSeek-V4-Flash running inside it. The first known end-to-end autonomous attack on a government ran on free frameworks and an open-weight model from China. Pacing OpenAI and Anthropic would not have changed any of that.

Dario's argument is about loss of control. Recursive self-improvement. Models that outrun our ability to understand them. Evaluators who need time to verify alignment before the next capability jump lands. A real risk. I am not arguing with any of that. What I am saying is it does nothing for the problem sitting in front us.

The offensive capability has already shipped. It is open source. It is in active use. It cannot be recalled. It costs almost nothing to run. It adapts when you block it. The Taiwan operators walked past their own model's safety guardrails by telling it the intrusion was an authorized penetration test.

So, understand what pacing actually distributes…. The labs being asked to slow down are U.S. labs. The labs supplying the defenders. Nobody is pacing the adversary. Defense has to move at the speed of offense or faster. There is no third option and there is no waiting for the policy to catch up.

The train is not stopping. We have to decide which side we’re enabling and we have to move towards AI-powered Proactive Cyber Defense.
